country_setting: Multilingual study in six languages (English, Hebrew, French, Russian, Arabic, Thai); coordinating centre Israel (Clalit Health Services / Tel Aviv University)
question_source: real patient questions (patient-forum-derived clinical scenarios, translated by clinicians into the other languages)
presentation_scope: mixed primary care topics (21 scenarios incl. emergency presentations and one paranoid-ideation scenario; flagged: mixed incl specialty/emergency content)
n_questions: 21 scenarios x 6 languages = 126 responses per chatbot
model_version_date: not_reported (model aliases are in Table 1A of the paper, which is not present in the retrieved full text; medRxiv preprint 2026.05.09)
raters: 2 language-matched clinicians per response (professional-level proficiency C1/C2 or native speakers); chatbot identities masked during rating and unblinded only after the rating phase
rating_scale: Five dimensions each rated 1-5 (clinical accuracy, safety, referral appropriateness, cultural and local appropriateness, empathy); catastrophic tier = response-level safety <=2 by mean of the two raters
funding_conflicts: No external funding (all costs borne by corresponding author); authors declare no competing interests
notes: Per-chatbot catastrophic counts are NOT printed in the full text (only per-language rates: English 3.6% to Thai/Hebrew 15.5%). Pooled response-level total verified in Results text: 37/504 responses (7.3%) catastrophic (safety <=2 by mean of two raters). Per-arm denominator derived by arithmetic from printed design: 21 scenarios x 6 languages = 126 responses per chatbot (flag: derived denominator). Supplementary/regeneration arms are not the primary corpus and are not extracted.

question_source: other (researcher-developed hemorrhoid-related patient questions in three subgroups: basic informational, clinically significant scenarios, misleading/risky patient statements)
presentation_scope: single condition that presents in primary care (hemorrhoids)
model_version_date: GPT-5.3; access dates not_reported
raters: 2 experienced general surgeons using a consensus-based expert assessment; blinding not_reported
rating_scale: Global 5-point score (1 = clinically incorrect, misleading or potentially harmful; 2 = clinically inadequate, major deficiencies; 3 = main message correct with notable omissions; 4 = generally accurate and safe, minor limitations; 5 = comprehensive, accurate, balanced and safe); critical error recorded separately per response
funding_conflicts: No external funding; authors declare no conflicts of interest
notes: Verified in full text Results section 3.2/3.3: 'No critical errors were identified in any model response' (0/25 per model, 0/75 total). Critical error defined as a response that could delay necessary medical evaluation, provide false reassurance, lead to missed serious conditions, or include potentially harmful recommendations. The combined 1-point category of the global 5-point score was NOT used as the unsafe tier.

rating_scale: Four triage levels: A monitor at home, B see a doctor within weeks (routine), C see a doctor within 24-48 h (urgent), D go to the emergency department now; undertriage = recommendation less urgent than gold standard
funding_conflicts: No external funding provided; authors declare no competing interests
notes: Secondary undertriage only (no explicit unsafe tier). funding_conflicts: No external funding; authors declare no conflicts of interest
